It's not to find if she had classified data on her home server... we all know she did, and the FBI said she did.

See, when a trial happens, all evidence has to become public domain... this is the basis of an open/fair trial. If the release of evidence doesn't happen, you end up with backroom trials, with closed doors, and no justification for punishment. In essence, if the judge, attorneys, and jury operate behind closed doors and sentence you to death, wouldn't you like to know why?

The rub is that this evidence is classified material. So, in order to submit it as evidence, it has to be declassified and placed in the public domain, for all to see. If the E-mails are "TOO" classified, and aren't ready to be released, then the government won't press charges because they don't have any evidence to submit. But, with the Wiki-leaks release of many of the E-mails, with the rest just over the horizon, this has become a moot point.
